VERDICT: DISAGREE.

I want to say first that the FUNCTIONAL change in this pull request is correct, minimal,
and exactly what it says it is -- I proved that mechanically, below, and it is the
strongest thing in its favour. It fails on how it was delivered, not on what it decided.

=== NEAR-MISS I AM PRINTING, AND IT CORRECTS MY OWN EARLIER WORK TODAY ===
I was about to charge this pull request with `lwb-check-state-claims` being red. IT IS RED,
but I checked the base before writing it down:
  on a PRISTINE origin/main checkout (bfe8507): python scripts/lwb_check_state_claims.py --repo .
    -> FAIL: HANDOFF.md:44: [stale main SHA in generated block] f9b4dea (live: bfe8507)
  git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -> this PR does not touch HANDOFF.md at all.
So main is red on that check by itself: merging any PR advances main past the sha its own
HANDOFF block recorded. This is NOT this pull request's defect and I do not count it.
It also qualifies what I wrote about #29 and #32 earlier in this same run, where I listed
the same failure as blocking without saying that the base carries it too. On those
branches it is red in HANDOFF content those PRs DO modify, and it does block their merge,
so the finding stands -- but "the base is red the same way" is context those records
should have carried and did not. I am recording the correction here and posting it on both
of those pull requests rather than leaving it only in this file.

=== B1 (BLOCKING, AND THE ACTUAL CAUSE OF THE RED `test` LEGS). No proof record. ===
  python scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --pr 40 --base origin/main --head HEAD
    -> FAIL: PR #40 carries no proof/*.json record for itself.
The `lwb-proof-pr` step in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs exactly this, so all six `test`
legs are red for this reason. I could not read the job logs (the log blob is 403 through
my proxy), so I reproduced every step of the `test` job locally instead of guessing:
pytest, lwb_build --check, both plugin validators, lwb-prefix, lwb-no-instruction-dep,
lwb-proof, HANDOFF shape and lwb-check-state-claims. Everything else in that job is green
here except the state-claims step, which the base also fails (see above). Owner directive
7: done means committed AND pushed WITH a proof record.

=== B2 (BLOCKING, AND PAINFULLY IRONIC). lwb-commit-identity is red on this PR's OWN
    content commits, and this PR's own fix does not save it. ===
  python scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base origin/main --head HEAD -> EXIT 1
    FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot:
          LEAPWare <300127941+LEAPWare-HQ@users.noreply.github.com>
All THREE content commits (54eb044, 3f6a2b5, 4793afc) carry that author. The name is
"LEAPWare" but ALLOWED_HUMAN is the PAIR ("LEAPWare", "leapware@outlook.com"), and the
address is the GitHub API's numeric noreply, which is not an allow-listed bot identity
either (BOT_NAME requires a `[bot]` suffix). The exemption this PR adds covers RECORD-ONLY
commits; these are content commits, so the fix does not exempt them. The pull request that
exists to stop the identity check from permanently redding branches is permanently redded
by the identity check, and force-push is denied. This is the third open pull request I
found today killed by a commit identity, and the first where the offending commits are the
PR's own content rather than a reviewer's bookkeeping.

=== B3 (BLOCKING). BOTH behaviour changes are completely untested. ===
This is the finding I would keep if I could keep only one, because it is about a change to
the MERGE GATE ITSELF.
  git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -c '^tests/'  ->  0
MUTATION PROBE, both changes reverted in the working tree at once:
  - `_id_segments`: dropped the `and seg.lower() not in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS` filter
  - `_authors`: removed the `if _is_record_only_commit(sha): continue` skip
  python -m pytest tests/ -q  ->  522 passed
NOT ONE TEST NOTICED. Both edits were restored; the tree was clean before I wrote this.
So a future regression reverting either change is invisible to CI, and neither behaviour
is pinned by anything. This repository has a written history of shipping vacuous checks
and then finding them; here there is no check at all. Two tests would fix it: one asserting
two ids sharing only "buildcraft" do NOT collide, one asserting a record-only commit with a
non-LEAPWare author passes while a content commit with the same author fails.

=== B4 (BLOCKING). The pull request body's claim about its own gate is FALSE at this head. ===
The body says: "Since this is `LWB-Agent: human`, `lwb-lanes` skips shared-path review per
its own existing rule."
  python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr-number 40 -> EXIT 1
    FAIL: f170d4ec507f: touches a shared path and has 0 independent review(s) in reviews/40/
The claim was true for the three human-trailered content commits. It stopped being true
when f170d4e landed: that is reviewer B's own record-only commit, it carries
`LWB-Agent: claude`, and `reviews/` is a shared path -- so the act of filing a review
created a review requirement that the filed DISAGREE then failed. A reviewer cannot review
this pull request without making it need a review. Compounded by what I measured on #32 in
this same run: `_review_ok` appends a non-AGREE record to `errors` (before the staleness
test) and `main()` returns 1 if errors is non-empty, so that DISAGREE now reds `lwb-lanes`
here permanently, and so does mine. I file it anyway; a false AGREE is worse.

=== WHAT I PROVED IN THIS PULL REQUEST'S FAVOUR, and it is substantial ===
The diffstat looks alarming -- 228 deletions against 83 insertions in scripts/lwb_lanes.py,
the file that IS the merge gate. I did not trust the diff's shape either way. I parsed both
versions, stripped docstrings, normalised with ast.unparse and diffed the result:
  scripts/lwb_lanes.py            -> 11 diff lines: IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS added, and the one
                                     `_id_segments` set comprehension gains the filter.
  scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py -> 20 diff lines: the import, `%H` added to the git
                                     log format, and the `_is_record_only_commit` skip.
THAT IS ALL. The functional change is precisely the two fixes the body describes and
nothing else is hidden in those 228 deleted lines. I also confirmed `_id_segments` is
called only by `_shared_long_segment`, so the new filter is scoped to the collision check
and does not touch id-format parsing. And I verified the false positive it fixes is real:
on PR #39's branch, restoring the `buildcraft` segment in commit_author_id makes lwb-lanes
fail with "share the segment 'buildcraft' (10 characters ...)". The decision in this pull
request is right. That is why I am recording the delivery problems instead of the design.

=== NON-BLOCKING, BUT DO NOT LET IT PASS UNREMARKED ===
(a) scripts/lwb_lanes.py goes from 845 lines to 658. 187 lines of recorded reasoning are
    deleted -- 76 comment lines plus docstrings -- and the body describes this change as
    "Two fixes" without mentioning it. Every em-dash in the file became `--` as well, which
    is the signature of a whole-file rewrite rather than a surgical edit, consistent with
    3f6a2b5's own message about a `create_or_update_file` placeholder mistake. In a
    repository whose comments are its institutional memory, each one recording a measured
    defect, that deletion is a bigger change than either fix. Among the casualties:
    `_is_record_only_commit`'s note that an EMPTY commit must not be vacuously record-only,
    `resolve_head_sha`'s note that it returns None so callers fail loudly instead of
    silently skipping the freshness check, and the explanation of why generated vendor
    output is shared rather than lane-owned.
(b) One deletion is load-bearing ACROSS pull requests: the `_review_ok` comment reading
    "recorded and surfaced, never trusted as proof" is gone, and
    reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md -- the entire subject of open PR #32 -- quotes that
    comment VERBATIM as one of the three places the repository already said so. If both
    land in either order, #32's citation dangles.
(c) The identity exemption means nothing now checks WHO authors a review record, and review
    records are the merge gate's evidence. The PR calls them "pure bookkeeping"; they are
    the bookkeeping the gate reads. I think the exemption is still right -- the alternative
    is the deadlock it fixes -- but that consequence belongs in writing somewhere.
(d) "lwb" in IGNORED_ID_SEGMENTS is dead: at 3 characters it can never reach
    MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH = 8. Harmless, but it reads as protection it does not provide.
